title: Bangladesh extends loan relief deadline for raw jute exporters
summary:
Bangladesh Bank has given raw jute exporters until September 30, 2026 to seek restructuring of classified loans with a 2 per cent down payment.
Banks have until December 31, 2026 to settle applications under unchanged BRPD circular terms.
The move gives distressed jute shippers more time to regularise accounts amid sector-specific financial pressures.

title: Turkiye’s fabric imports fall 8.3% in January–July 2026
summary:
Turkiye’s fabric imports fell 8.3 per cent year on year to $978.502 million in January–July 2026, from $1.067 billion a year earlier.
China remained the largest supplier, with shipments up 7.7 per cent to $311.971 million and share rising to 31.88 per cent.
Imports from Egypt fell 47.9 per cent to $119.290 million, moving it from second to third among suppliers.

title: EU's maritime transport leads goods trade by volume in 2025
summary:
European Union sea imports reached 1.1 billion tonnes worth €1,270 billion (~$1.44 trillion) in 2025, while seaborne exports totalled 0.5 billion tonnes worth €1,069 billion (~$1.21 trillion).
Maritime transport carried over 72 per cent of the bloc's goods trade by weight.
Air and road took smaller volume shares but higher-value cargo, shaping modal choices for sourcing and logistics teams.

title: Australia's unemployment rises to 4.6% in August
summary:
Australia’s seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose to 4.6 per cent in August, despite employment increasing by 39,000 people, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS). 
Part-time jobs rose by 46,000, while full-time employment fell by 6,000. 
The participation rate increased to 67.1 per cent, while underemployment eased to 6.2 per cent.

title: EU eases import duties on Armenian goods for 2 years
summary:
EU ministers have adopted temporary trade-liberalisation measures covering around 80 per cent of Armenian exports to the EU for two years.
The move is meant to support Armenia after recent Russian trade restrictions and strengthen Armenia-EU trade flows.
Importers get lower duties across a broad product range, including certain agricultural goods.
Safeguards remain if imports hurt EU producers.

title: Bangladesh eases MMF imports: A new route for synthetic apparel?
summary:
Bangladesh has eased imports of specialised synthetic fabrics for seamless sportswear, high-value fashion items and functional apparel.
Its RMG exports reached $38.70 billion in FY2025–26, or 80.62 per cent of total exports, while most MMF yarns and fibres are imported.
US apparel shipments from Bangladesh were about $4.66 billion in January–July 2026, down 6.5 per cent year on year.

title: Canada, Vietnam strengthen trade ties under new Strategic Partnership
summary:
Canada and Vietnam have elevated bilateral ties to a Strategic Partnership, with trade, investment, economic co-operation, transportation and supply-chain management among its core areas. 
Both sides reaffirmed support for concluding the ASEAN-Canada FTA and strengthening co-operation under the CPTPP.
Vietnam is Canada’s largest trading partner in ASEAN, highlighting the scope for further trade.

title: Asia freight diverges: Europe gains an ocean-freight cost advantage
summary:
On September 24, a 40-foot container from Shanghai to New York cost $10,373, against $3,485 to Rotterdam; the $6,888 gap is more than twice early July's spread.
Shanghai–New York was flat; Los Angeles rose 2 per cent, while Rotterdam fell 4 per cent and Genoa 5 per cent.
The gap offers sourcing teams a shipment window, not a basis for long-term freight commitments.

title: Weakness persists in south Indian cotton yarn, prices down in Mumbai
summary:
South Indian cotton yarn market stayed bearish, with Mumbai prices down ₹2–4 per kg amid selling pressure, poor payment conditions and cautious buying.
Tiruppur cotton yarn prices held steady after earlier declines, though mills faced pressure from subdued export demand and falling ICE cotton.
Gujarat cotton fell ₹1,000 per candy as delayed new-crop arrivals were offset by ICE cotton volatility.

title: Bangladesh gets RCEP go-ahead as accession process moves forward
summary:
Bangladesh has received approval to advance its accession process to RCEP, with an ad hoc working group to expedite negotiations. 
For apparel and textile supply chains, membership could expand access to major Asian-Pacific markets, help address post-LDC graduation trade challenges, retain preferential market access, strengthen supply-chain integration and attract foreign direct investment (FDI).

title: Fashion’s climate push: Clean power becomes a supplier capability
summary:
Levi Strauss & Co. and Marks & Spencer launched the Fashion Renewable Collaborative in New York to help mills and factories access renewable electricity.
Cascale’s Athens meeting put financing, accountability and business value at the centre of supply-chain transformation.
The platform combines supplier-energy programmes and supports power purchase agreements, certificates, on-site generation.

title: Japan’s apparel imports grow 6.6% to $2.3 bn in July 2026
summary:
Japan's apparel and accessories imports rose 6.6 per cent year on year to 371,963 million yen (~$2.36 billion) in August 2026.
Textile yarn and fabric imports climbed 16.9 per cent, while exports grew 10.4 per cent during the month.
Textile machinery exports rose 24.0 per cent to 27,984 million yen in August and 11.7 per cent to 160,129 million yen in January-June 2026.

title: EU Philippines FTA opens €514 mn apparel sourcing opportunity
summary:
EU-Philippines FTA talks reached substantial agreement on September 22, 2026, with over 94 per cent of tariff lines expected to be liberalised.
TexPro shows H1 2026 EU27 imports from the Philippines up 45.8 per cent in HS6110 sweaters, 16.7 per cent in HS6203 and 10.0 per cent in HS6204.
Rules of origin, capacity and compliance will decide if preferential access becomes durable EU business.

title: Luxury demand polarises: How is the fashion supply chain responding?
summary:
First-half 2026 results show luxury demand concentrating at the top end as higher prices and softer discretionary spending curb aspirational buyers.
Prada Group revenue rose 16 per cent at constant exchange rates to €3.048 billion (~$3.46 billion), while Hermès grew 6.1 per cent.
Moncler EMEA, Ferragamo wholesale and Gucci show pressure, prompting reassessment of pricing, product mix and distribution.

title: New Look, M&S, Sainsbury’s, Oxfam launch UK textile recycling plan
summary:
New Look, M&S, Sainsbury’s, Oxfam and Circle-8 have announced The Circuit to build UK circular textile value chains.
It will recover, sort and pre-process non-reusable end-of-use textiles into feedstock for fibre to fibre recycling.
The first phase starts in January 2027 at Oxfam’s Batley site, testing automated sorting, traceability and scale-up models.

title: Climate Pledge Fashion Coalition targets net zero fashion by 2040
summary:
The Climate Pledge, Amazon, Stella McCartney and Canopy have launched a Fashion Coalition, with World Economic Forum support, to help more than 60 signatories reach net-zero carbon by 2040.
The group will aggregate demand, develop blended finance and offer tools intended to commercialise lower-carbon materials, technologies and supply chains.

title: Global supply shifts open growth window for Indian apparel: Report
summary:
India held about 3 per cent of global apparel exports in 2025, while China’s share fell to 27.3 per cent from 36.9 per cent in 2010, PL Capital said.
Bangladesh and Vietnam have captured more of the shift, lifting their combined share to over 13 per cent.
Trade access, China+1 sourcing and policy support could favour large, integrated Indian garment exporters.

title: China gains as Bangladesh loses share in Denmark apparel market
summary:

China’s shipments rose 5.4 per cent to $568.519 million, lifting its share to 21.91 per cent; Bangladesh fell 13.1 per cent to $438.509 million.
Germany stayed third, Sweden moved close behind and Poland ranked fifth as the top five suppliers held 62.81 per cent of imports.

title: New Zealand’s apparel imports rise 5.8% in August 2026
summary:

January–August imports slipped 0.7 per cent to NZ$1.377 billion as the decline narrowed from 1.6 per cent.
Knitted or crocheted fabric imports fell 12.4 per cent in August but rose 12.5 per cent in January–August.
Apparel exports fell 5.8 per cent in August, though January–August exports edged up 0.1 per cent.

title: Pearl Global commissions new garment manufacturing unit in Bangladesh
summary:
Pearl Global Industries has commissioned a new garment facility and expanded sustainable laundry capacity in Bangladesh. 
The unit adds about 7 million pieces of annual garment capacity, taking total installed capacity to about 108 million pieces per annum. 
The laundry expansion is expected to improve efficiency, reduce washing costs and water use, and generate ROCE of about 18-20 per cent.
